title: Working at Redwood: Employee Experience, Roles & Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring and Onboarding, and Internal Tools Guide
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview

This handbook page consolidates core guidance for working at Redwood: our values and day-to-day expectations, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks summary, hiring and onboarding routines, and the set of internal tools most new hires use. It is intended for all employees and managers and is maintained by People Ops with engineering and product collaborators.

Sections
1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations
2) Roles & career ladders — how we define levels and growth paths
3) Benefits & perks — summary and enrollment steps
4) Hiring & onboarding overview — hiring principles and new-hire checklist
5) Internal tools guide — quick starts and ownership

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations\nIntro
Redwood is a developer-first company focused on reliable, cost-efficient LLM inference. We value ownership, clarity, and operational rigor. Employees are expected to: ship reliably, prioritize user-facing quality (latency, cost, reliability), and collaborate across product, engineering, and GTM. Managers are expected to provide clear goals, career guidance, and timely feedback.

Core principles
- Ship measurable outcomes: define metrics (SLOs, cost/unit) and measure impact.
- Shared ownership: services and customer outcomes are owned by teams, not individuals.
- Developer empathy: prioritize DX and ergonomics when making tradeoffs.
- Operational readiness: every change must include an observability plan and rollback strategy.

Working norms
- Asynchronous-first communication: document decisions in Confluence and use Slack for short-lived coordination.
- Weekly cadences: weekly team sync + cross-team triage for critical issues.
- On-call: rotations for production services; SRE-run playbooks define runbook steps and escalation.
- Meeting culture: agenda + outcome required; prefer async reviews for design documents.

2) Roles & career ladders — how we define levels and growth paths\nOverview
We use role families (Engineering, Product, Research, SRE, DX, People Ops, Sales) with leveled ladders that describe scope, impact, and expected behaviors. Career conversations are driven by calibrated performance reviews and one-on-one development plans.

Role family snapshot (examples)
- Engineering: IC1 (New grad/Entry) → IC2 (Mid) → IC3 (Senior) → IC4 (Staff) → IC5 (Principal)
- Product: PM1 → PM2 → PM3 → PM4 (Lead)
- SRE: SRE1 → SRE2 → SRE3 → SRE4

Level expectations (summary table)
| Level | Scope | Impact | Examples of deliverables |
|-------|-------|--------|-------------------------|
| IC2 (Mid) | Component ownership | Delivers features end-to-end | Implements API endpoints, writes unit/integration tests |
| IC3 (Senior) | Service ownership & mentoring | Improves reliability or latency by measurable % | Leads major rollouts, owns major production incidents postmortem |
| IC4 (Staff) | Cross-team initiatives | Sets technical strategy and drives adoption | Designs cross-cutting runtime/kernel optimizations, authors ADRs |

Promotion process (high-level)
1. Employee and manager agree goals and evidence for promotion over a 6-12 month horizon.
2. Manager submits packet with examples (PRs, incidents, design docs, metrics).
3. Calibration panel (peers + senior leadership) reviews and provides recommendation.
4. People Ops communicates outcome and next steps.

Development planning
- Quarterly career plan: 3-5 concrete goals, success metrics, mentoring assignments.
- Manager responsibilities: provide stretch work, feedback cycles, and visibility to cross-team opportunities.

3) Benefits & perks — summary and enrollment steps\nBenefits summary (core offerings)
| Category | What Redwood provides | Enrollment notes |
|----------|----------------------|------------------|
| Health & dental | Multiple medical plans, dental, vision | Enroll within 30 days of start; carrier details in Workday Benefits tab |
| Parental leave | 18 weeks primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary | Submit request to People Ops 60 days prior where possible |
| Retirement | 401(k) with 4% company match | Auto-enroll; manage contributions in payroll portal |
| Remote & flexibility | Hybrid offices, remote-first roles, $1,200 WFH stipend | Stipend request form in internal tools (Trello/Concur link) |
| Learning & development | $2,000 annual L&D budget; 2 paid conference days | Request via L&D portal; manager pre-approval required |
| Wellness | Monthly wellness stipend, EAP | Details in Benefits FAQ page |

How to enroll
1. Complete benefits enrollment in Workday within 30 days of start.
2. For pre-tax commuter or flexible spending: submit elections in payroll portal.
3. For one-time stipends (WFH, relocation): open a request in the Finance portal with manager approval.

Benefits contacts
- People Ops Benefits Lead: benefits@redwood.ai (primary contact)
- Payroll questions: payroll@redwood.ai

4) Hiring & onboarding overview — hiring principles and new-hire checklist\nHiring principles
- Hire for long-term potential and role fit; diversify candidate slates.
- Define clear scorecards before sourcing.
- Structured interviews: use calibrated rubrics, include a take-home or live technical exercise where appropriate.
- Inclusion: all interviewers must complete bias and inclusive hiring training.

Interview stages (typical for engineering)
1. Recruiter screen (30m): role fit, compensation expectations, timeline.
2. Technical screen (45m): system design or coding exercise.
3. On-site loop (3-5 interviews): design, implementation, collaboration, product sense.
4. Offer & compensation: manager + recruiter finalize package; People Ops issues official offer.

New-hire onboarding checklist (90-day)
Pre-start (Recruiter/Manager)
- Offer signed and paperwork completed in Workday.
- Hardware ordered (laptop, monitors) and shipped — eng infra owner: infra-ops@redwood.ai.
- Accounts created in Okta, GitHub, Slack, Confluence.

Day 1-7
- Day 1: Welcome meeting with manager and People Ops; set up accounts; complete benefits enrollment.
- Complete security training and required compliance modules.
- Join team standups and meet buddy/mentor.

First 30 days
- Complete product and platform orientation (runtime, routing, console).
- Pair with teammate on a small ticket; submit first PR with reviewer feedback.
- 1:1 weekly with manager; complete 30-day onboarding survey.

60-90 days
- Drive a small-to-medium scoped project to production or feature-complete state.
- Career check-in with manager; update 90-day goals and L&D plan.

Onboarding roles and responsibilities
- Manager: owns role clarity, first 90-day plan, and check-ins.
- Buddy: day-to-day questions, tooling orientation.
- People Ops: benefits, payroll, compliance, and new-hire logistics.

5) Internal tools guide — quick starts and ownership\nCore systems and quick-start commands
- Identity & SSO: Okta — use SSO to access Confluence, Slack, GitHub.
- Source control: GitHub (org: redwood-inference). Create PRs into main, use branch naming: team/issue-123-description.
- CI/CD: CircleCI + internal build agents. Key commands: `make test`, `make image`, `circleci local execute`.
- Issue tracking & roadmap: Jira — create tickets using team templates; label by component and priority.
- Docs: Confluence — use page templates for runbooks, ADRs, design docs. Include owner and status metadata on each page.
- Observability: Datadog + internal traces. Dashboards: engineering/dashboards -> latency, error-rate, cost-per-token.
- Incident comms: PagerDuty for on-call; use the incident template in Confluence for postmortems.

Tool access & approvals
- New hires automatically get baseline access via Okta.
- Additional access (prod clusters, customer vaults) requires manager approval and completion of security training. Submit requests via the Access Request form in Confluence.

Common onboarding tasks (commands and links)
- Clone core repos: `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/runtime.git`
- Local dev quickstart: follow repo README: `make dev-start` -> starts local services on ports 8080/9090.
- Run unit tests: `make test` and `pytest -k <module>`
- Telemetry: request a Datadog onboarding runbook from eng-platform.

Ownership and documentation expectations
- Every service must have: owner(s), runbook link, on-call rotation, SLOs, and cost dashboard. Use the service template in Confluence when creating new services.
- ADRs required for infra, public API, and runtime kernel changes. Link ADRs from the service page and include roll-forward and rollback plans.
